title: Full AES-256 key recovery conditional on a weak related-key pair, BKN 2009 encryption/decryption variant

target.description: Standard full AES-256 key recovery using Section 4.2's first and second steps, conditional on a related-key pair satisfying the weak key-schedule trail.

setting.key_relation: Fixed master-key XOR relation K and K XOR DeltaK; the Appendix A key-schedule differential imposes five probability-2^-7 S-box transitions.
setting.key_population: A qualifying weak related-key pair, whose incidence is estimated as 2^-35; pair discovery is outside this conditional record.
setting.plaintext_model: Two 2^64 chosen-plaintext structures per first-step repetition, followed by chosen-ciphertext pairs with the specified output difference for the second step.
assumptions: Encryption and decryption under the selected weak pair are available.
The first step's 80 recovered bits are available to filter the chosen-ciphertext pairs in the second step.
The final 96-bit exhaustive search is included; this is not only an 80-bit partial-key result.

time.note: The first step costs 2^96 data and time for one pair, and the final search costs 2^96 steps. Section 6 explicitly summarizes 2^96 time for the weak-key attack. This is the source's dominant-order estimate, not an exact sum of equal-exponent stages.

data.reported: 2^96 encryption queries plus 2^91 decryption queries; dominant order 2^96
data.note: Section 4.2 p.243 repeats two 2^64-text structures 2^31 times, totaling 2^96 encryptions across the pair; the second step decrypts 2^90 ciphertext pairs, totaling 2^91 decryptions. Table 1's per-key shorthand is not multiplied by two again.

memory.note: Table 1 and Section 6 report 2^65 for the key-recovery attack. The first-step-only 2^64 figure on p.243 is not substituted for the overall summary; no storage-unit conversion is asserted.

preprocessing.note: No separately reusable preprocessing budget is stated for this selected encryption/decryption attack.

success.description: No numerical full-master-key recovery success is supplied. This endpoint is conditional on a qualifying weak pair; acquiring that pair is not included in its primary event. The first stage expects four right pairs,2^31 wrong pairs and2^47 random80-bit votes. The CCA second stage expects eight right pairs and then prices the remaining12 bytes by2^96 exhaustive search. The source no-wrong-survivor wording does not quantify joint acquisition, uniqueness and full-key output. Expected counts are not converted into primary probabilities.

components.description: Section4.2 first step: remaining state-trail probability after the structured first two rounds, conditional on an actual qualifying key pair.

Section4.2: source assigns2^(64-93)=2^-29 to a structure producing a right pair. Retain this as its local first-moment approximation;2^31 repetitions give mean four, not an independently established end-to-end success distribution.

Section4.2 second step: the source relaxes one2^-6 transition, giving2^-87 for the remaining rounds, conditional on the weak pair and correct first-stage80-bit material. Its2^90 chosen ciphertext pairs give expected eight, not a new primary success.

Section4.2 second step:48-bit partial-encryption filter using correctly recovered first-stage material, reducing2^90 pairs to2^42 source candidates. This filter is not an overall wrong-key or full-key success probability.

review.scope: Exact-edition endpoint-specific success audit. Local pair filters, conditional trails, weak-pair incidence and expected counts keep their own experiment; correlation is not a decision probability. Existing conflicts, resources, targets, settings and full-audit gates remain unchanged.

evidence.locator: Section 4.1 p.242; Section 4.2 First step pp.242-243 and Second step pp.243-244; Section 6 p.245; Table 1 p.233.
evidence.interpretation: The conditional result removes only the outer scan over 2^35 candidate related-key pairs. Both recovery stages and the final 96-bit exhaustive search remain, supporting a full-key goal with encryption/decryption oracles.

evidence.locator: Section 4.2 p.243, numbered first-step procedure and the paragraph beginning 'Second step'; p.244, final exhaustive-search sentence.
evidence.interpretation: The explicit algorithm fixes pair-wide oracle totals and the chosen-ciphertext requirement. Power-of-two totals are leading estimates, not exact accounting of all lower-order work or query terms.

limitations: This conditional two-key record does not include finding a qualifying pair and is not an arbitrary designated-key attack.
The chosen-ciphertext second stage cannot be used with encryption-only access; the paper's alternative TA completion has a different cost.
The source's per-key table labels are less precise than its pair-based procedure; normalization follows the explicit procedure.
No independent recovery or full resource-accounting reproduction was performed.
